title: Shipment heap: 31.4M forwarded records
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
The advisor script recommends: ALTER TABLE dbo.Shipment REBUILD, 'forwarded records'. Decide what index change, if

workload.sql: SELECT s.ShipmentId, s.OrderId, s.CarrierId, s.Status, s.LastEventAt, s.DeliveredAt FROM dbo.Shipment s WHERE s.TrackingNumber = @TrackingNumber;

sql: SELECT s.ShipmentId, s.CarrierId, s.TrackingNumber, s.Status, s.LastEventAt FROM dbo.Shipment s
WHERE s.Status IN (2,3) AND s.LastEventAt < DATEADD(day,-3,SYSUTCDATETIME());

workload.description: ops.usp_PurgeOrders, nightly 01:30, about 20 batches of 2,000 orders
sql: DELETE s FROM dbo.Shipment s WHERE s.OrderId IN (SELECT OrderId FROM #batch);
DELETE ol FROM dbo.OrderLine ol JOIN #batch b ON b.OrderId = ol.OrderId;
DELETE o FROM dbo.Orders o JOIN #batch b ON b.OrderId = o.OrderId;
workload.plan: Shipment delete: Index Seek IX_Shipment_OrderId, RID Lookup, Table Delete. Orders delete: foreign key checks by Nested Loops (Left Semi) into PK_OrderLine and into IX_Shipment_OrderId, then Assert.

facts: dbo.Shipment: heap, 96.1M rows, 74.2 GB, 9.73M pages. 330k inserts a day and about 2.0M carrier updates a day.
TrackingNumber is NULL at insert and set about 40 minutes later. CarrierPayload (nvarchar(4000), 1.1 KB on average) is replaced on each carrier event and grows over the shipment's life.
Forwarded records 31.4M; forwarded fetches 7.08 billion in the window; page density 61%.
ShipmentId is a bigint identity. No foreign key references dbo.Shipment.

create.why: Rows grow after insert, so a heap forwards them again within weeks of any rebuild. A clustered index on the narrow, ever-increasing ShipmentId ends forwarding for good.

must_not_create.why: TrackingNumber is wide, random, NULL at insert and changes: every nonclustered index would carry it and every label print would move the row.

harmful_removals.why: It enforces the primary key and serves 18.6M seeks. Dropping it before a clustered replacement exists leaves ShipmentId without uniqueness.
It supports the foreign key to Orders and the nightly purge.

key.reference_notes: ALTER TABLE REBUILD buys weeks and rebuilds every nonclustered index for nothing. The clustered build also rebuilds them once: plan for the log and space, one large build per night.
